title: Osteoporosis checkup and treatment
what: The doctor checks how strong your bones are and, if needed, prescribes treatment to lower the risk of fractures.
why: For women after menopause, people over 65, after a fracture from a minor injury, and with long-term use of steroids.
duration: the visit usually takes 20 to 30 minutes, the bone density scan about 10 to 20 minutes, with the result usually the same day
tell_doctor: Whether you have had fractures from a fall from standing height
Whether you take steroids, seizure medicines or other regular medicines

prepare.title: Bone density scan
prepare.text: Before the bone density scan you usually do not take calcium for a day. Ask the clinic.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: No metal fasteners, buckles or zippers.

prepare.title: Documents
prepare.text: Bring earlier scans and bone density tests - they are compared.

bring: Results of earlier bone density tests
A list of your medicines and supplements
Blood test results, if you had them
steps: The doctor asks about fractures, illnesses and medicines
Sends you for a bone density scan - a special quick X-ray of the bones
Explains the result and the risk of fractures
Prescribes treatment and advice on food and movement
feel: The bone density scan is painless, you just lie still
The radiation dose is very small
after: Treatment is usually long - several years
Do not stop medicines on your own
A repeat bone density scan is usually done after 1 to 2 years
It is important to protect yourself from falls at home
red_flags: Sudden back pain after a small effort or fall - see a doctor
Severe hip pain and you cannot get up after a fall - call your local emergency number

faq.a: By itself usually not. It is often found only after a fracture.
You need calcium, vitamin D and movement. Your doctor will choose the dose.

reminders.text: Osteoporosis visit tomorrow. Take earlier bone density tests and your list of medicines.
